      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Include m_net in CService printer so IPv6 and CJDNS with identical bytes do not print identically",

participants.note: Concept ACK and asked about exhaustiveness of callsite conversions

claims.text: Header drags addrman, key_io, and protocol into tests that do not need them, increasing preprocessed lines and causing unnecessary recompilations
claims.quote: feefrac_tests and txgraph_tests only need the FeeFrac printers, but this block drags addrman, key_io and protocol in with it. Touching addrman now rebuilds both, and it's about 12k extra preprocessed lines in the first one. Would it be worth splitting this by area?
claims.status_note: Author moved implementations to common.cpp with forward declarations in common.h
claims.status_by_quote: Added common.cpp with the implementations and all forward delc to common.h in latest push

claims.text: Printers omit fields compared by operator==, causing failed checks to display identical values or generic types without diagnostic detail
claims.quote: This one leaves out nTime and nServices, which operator== does compare, so in the two addrv1/addrv2 unserialize checks a regression in time or in flags comes out as [::1]:0 != [::1]:0. The CTxDestination one prints CTxDestination() for CNoDestination and PubKeyDestination. Worth checking each printer against the type's operator==?
claims.status_note: Author added missing fields to CAddress and CTxDestination printers
claims.status_by_quote: Added additional info for CAddress and took a glance through the rest of the ==, I think all fields should be covered. As far as CTxDestination, I added specific displays for each variant

claims.text: Encode asserts on an empty key, causing bip32_tests to abort with SIGABRT instead of reporting failure and continuing the suite
claims.quote: Encode() asserts on an empty key, which is what DecodeExtKey leaves you with when it fails, and that's the value bip32_tests compares. I broke the decode to see. The case dies on SIGABRT and takes the following ones with it. On master the same break just prints 17 failures and the suite finishes. Worth a guard here and in the CExtPubKey one?
claims.status_note: Author added length and validity guards, verified by reviewer
claims.status_by_quote: Yes, that's what I meant. I broke the decode again and now it prints CExtKey(<invalid>) and the suite finishes, no SIGABRT.

claims.text: Include m_net in CService printer so IPv6 and CJDNS with identical bytes do not print identically
claims.quote: While checking the changes I noticed a small nit. CService's == compares m_net, which the printer doesn't show, so IPv6 and CJDNS with the same bytes come out identical.
claims.status_note: Author added net field to CService debug string
claims.status_by_quote: Added a net field to CService

claims.text: Move printer implementations to a cpp file with forward declarations in the header to reduce recompilations
claims.quote: Most of the functions can be just the signature and a fwd decl for the type, and the actual stringify can move to a cpp file? This saves re-compilation at least in the other cases
claims.status_note: Author moved implementations to common.cpp with forward declarations in common.h
claims.status_by_quote: Added common.cpp with the implementations and all forward delc to common.h in latest push

claims.text: De-template FeeFrac stream operator and move implementation to the source file
claims.quote: No need for separate template instantiations for each derived type... And then you can also move the implementation to the source file forward declare FeeFrac in the header.
claims.status_note: Author de-templated FeeFrac and ByRatioNegSize and moved implementations to source file
claims.status_by_quote: I de-templated ByRatioNegSize as well because the only intended and current use case is with FeeFrac. Updated in latest push.

claims.text: Handle std::pair printer generally or move it to the test to avoid unnecessary includes
claims.quote: Why is this pair thing needed? Seems to be a single test-only thing? So either this should be moved to that test, or maybe pair should be handled generally, like the existing optional
claims.status_note: Author generalized std::pair stream operator with concepts constraint
claims.status_by_quote: I added a requires requires(std::ostream& os, const T& t, const U& u) { os << t; os << u; }, which I think it correct. Otherwise yeah this should be general, updated in latest push.

claims.text: Add contextual field labels in debug output representations
claims.quote: nit: add context to what we are displaying here and other places.
claims.status_note: Author applied field labels across debug printers
claims.status_by_quote: Makes sense. Applied those changes as well as adding a addr field to CService and CAddress.

claims.text: Add a comment in common.h describing the printable types for discoverability
claims.quote: Should we make common.h self-advertising so authors discover it without a reviewer? A short header comment listing the types it makes BOOST_CHECK_*-printable
claims.status_note: Author added header comment in common.h describing purpose and noting debug-available types
claims.status_by_quote: Added a comment to common.h describing the purpose of the file.

Add stream operator overload for CScript

claims.text: ScriptToAsmStr decodes small pushes as numbers, allowing scripts that differ in bytes to display identical string representations on failure

claims.status_note: Author added hex string alongside ASM representation

claims.text: Ask how exhaustive the conversion of BOOST_CHECK callsites is intended to be
claims.quote: How exhaustive is the conversion supposed to be? In this file alone there seem to be more cases where we compare scriptsigs.

claims.status_by_quote: It is intended to be completely exhaustive for the types with << added here. I ran the following: rg -nP ... which showed quite a few additional sites I missed that have been updated now
